chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idrees, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Hassan, from his uncle Abd al-Rahman ibn Katheer, from Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said:
I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام saying: “For the Master of this affair there will be two occultations; during one of them, he will return from it to his family,”
“and during the other, it will be said: ‘He perished in whichever valley he travelled in.’”
I said: “How should we act when it is like that?”
He said: “When a claimant claims it, then ask him about matters; he will answer concerning them like him.”

key_terms.أَشْيَاءَ: matters or questions used to test the claimant
key_terms.صَاحِبِ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ: the Master of this affair, referring to the divinely designated Imam
key_terms.غَيْبَتَانِ: two occultations or periods of concealment
key_terms.مُدَّعٍ: a claimant who makes a claim to the affair or authority
key_terms.هَلَكَ: it will be said that he perished

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the two occultations of the Imam and how to identify false claimants?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Sahib of this affair will have two ghaybahs, one in which he returns to his family and another in which people will think he has perished. It also instructs the believers on how to respond to false claimants during the period of occultation: they are to test such claimants through matters requiring the true knowledge of the rightful Imam. The narration is significant for Shia creed regarding the ghaybah and recognition of legitimate divine authority.
